title: Estonia 2007: a nation under digital siege

scenes.narration: [serious] In 2007, moving one statue set off cyberattacks on a country.
In April 2007, Estonia moved a Soviet war memorial from central Tallinn. Riots broke out.
On April 27, the attacks began. Floods of fake traffic jammed websites. That's DDoS, a traffic jam attack.
Government, bank and newspaper websites went down.
Another wave hit around May 9, Russia's Victory Day. The attacks lasted 22 days.
Estonia's foreign minister said much of it came from Russia. Moscow denied it. Proof never came.
Only one person was fined, a 20-year-old in Estonia. A whole country learned war can go online.

facts.claim: Estonia moved the Bronze Soldier, a Soviet WWII memorial, from central Tallinn; it sparked riots by ethnic Russians; Russia saw the move as an insult
DDoS attacks shut down government, newspaper and banking websites in waves: from April 27 peaking around May 3, and on May 8-9 around Russia's Victory Day
Foreign Minister Urmas Paet said the Kremlin was directly involved and much traffic came from Russia; Russia's EU ambassador Vladimir Chizhov denied it and said the claim had to be substantiated
Estonia suffered 22 days of cyberattacks in 2007 after the Bronze Soldier was moved; Estonia blamed Russia
Dmitri Galushkevich, 20, was fined about $1,620 for attacking the website of Prime Minister Andrus Ansip's Reform Party
